review_notes: No changes requested. Alternative inspected: adding a HasSum-based value lemma, e.g. `HasSum.tprod_one_add_eq (h : HasSum (∏ i ∈ ·, f i) a) : ∏' i, (1 + f i) = a`, next to the Summable-based `tprod_one_add`. Rejected because the PR already makes the HasSum -> HasProd step public as `hasProd_one_add_of_hasSum_prod`, and both other new lemmas in the submitted file use it. A caller who already knows the sum converges to `a` gets the value in one step with `(hasProd_one_add_of_hasSum_prod h).tprod_eq`, which is the usual HasX -> tX pattern in this file (compare `Summable.tsum_mul_left` via `(hf.hasSum.mul_left _).tsum_eq`). Neither the file nor the PR description shows a caller that needs a separate lemma. The order-bound comparison in operation.md does not apply: this section has no non-strict or strict bound lemmas. Assumptions checked: CommSemiring is required by `Finset.prod_one_add`. The lemmas correctly need no IsTopologicalSemiring, because the proof just composes with `tendsto_finset_powerset_atTop_atTop`. T2Space appears only where tsum/tprod uniqueness needs it. I also considered and rejected as preference: dot-notation names (`HasSum.hasProd_one_add`), shorter proof terms (`(hasProd_one_add_of_hasSum_prod h.hasSum).multipliable`), docstrings on the other two lemmas, and whether the new `BigOperators.Ring.Finset` import is redundant (it supplies `prod_one_add`, and the file compiles). There is no Mathlib checkout in the workspace, so I could not confirm the docstring cross-reference to `multipliable_one_add_of_summable`. I left it alone because docstring references do not affect compilation.
